title: test(verify, rest, create-objectstack): test budget slice 5, the warm-up docblock says what it shares and two rows run under 10 s
body:
Part of #23181
Clause-②: no

Slice 5 of the test-budget card (claim `6244488338`): the warm-up docblock correction carried by the slice 4 release (`6221486208`), the audit of slice 3's six warmed files, and the card's `@objectstack/rest` and `create-objectstack` rows, one file each. Test files and one test-layer helper only; nothing a package publishes moves, so `skip-changeset` rides this PR's create.

## Rows this PR closes

| row (card table) | card, CI (run) | newest refresh dry run `38897658479`, CI | isolated base median | isolated head median | runs | projected CI on the card's ratio / the newest window's ratio | claim |
|:--|--:|--:|--:|--:|:--|:--|:--|
| `create-objectstack` · `src/scaffold-e2e-boot-probe.test.ts` | 17.3 s (`38281387358`) | 15.72 s (`38858901527`) | 15345 ms | 6311 ms (−59%) | 3 interleaved rounds | 7.1 s / 6.5 s | **closed** |
| `@objectstack/rest` · `src/import-template-route.test.ts (local)` | 12.7 s (`38319885190`) | 16.81 s (`38877591164`) | 2572 ms | 1545 ms (−40%) | 4 interleaved rounds | 7.6 s / 10.1 s | **claimed on the card's ratio; on the newest window's ratio it sits at the line** |

The projection is the head median times the file's own CI ÷ isolated-base ratio. It is an estimate: the next landed refresh's list is the pin, and it decides both rows. For the `rest` row the ratio model is conservative in one known direction (part of what the head removes is first-load cost, which a cold, contended CI shard pays at a higher multiple than this box), and it is not a measurement of that direction.

**How each reading was taken.** Clocked = the vitest default-reporter file line (hooks plus tests, collection excluded), the number `report-test-timings.mjs` captures in CI; `AI_AGENT` and `CLAUDECODE` unset so vitest picks that reporter. Isolated = one `vitest run --maxWorkers=2` per file. Base = an untracked copy of the file beside it, blob-identical to the branch point `af284b05e` (`a5a23b161980`, `6b3163931e5a`), alternated with the head file round by round, every run through `os-verify-lock` on a 4-vCPU box shared with other agents. All copies were moved out before every commit.

- `rest`, base / head per round: r3 (head first) 2574 / 1593 · r4 (base first) 2570 / 1585 · r5 (head first) 2570 / 1454 · r6 (base first) 2713 / 1504. r6 is at the final bytes of the file; r3 to r5 ran on bytes that differ from them in one comment only.
- `create-objectstack`, base / head per round: ab2 (head first) 15345 / 6357 · ab3 (base first) 17296 / 6284 · ab4 (head first) 15329 / 6311. Ten more head runs at `451c13c48` (the file's final bytes): 14/14 passed in each, 6296 to 6360 ms.

## `create-objectstack`: the cases' own waits, summed

Measured per case (base, isolated): every case's wall is the waits of its own child processes, not this worker's work. The two `os start` blocks each cost one workflow-loop `sleep 2` (about 2.1 s) in the accept and fail-fast cases; the docker block's dying-container case 4.3 s (two loop sleeps on this box); the neighbour harness's "stayed alive" control its 2 s backstop; the other cases 3 to 230 ms. Run one after another, those waits summed to 15.3 s.

The waits are the subject (the workflow's own `run:` blocks, executed), so nothing waited on is shortened, stubbed or skipped. What changed is that they now overlap:

- `runBlock` awaits its `bash -e` child (`spawn`, stdio ignore / pipe / pipe, the same 240 s timeout) instead of blocking the worker in `execFileSync`. Its answer is the synchronous one's: the exit status (`-1` when a signal ended it, the timeout's included), stdout alone on success, stdout then stderr on failure.
- Both top-level suites pass vitest's `concurrent: true`. The cases share nothing: each has its own kernel-assigned port (held, never probed), harness directory and stub state. The 6.3 s is consistent with vitest's default `maxConcurrency` (5) starting the 4.3 s docker case after the first wave of about 2 s cases.

**One harness defect this exposed, fixed in the same file.** At `758aa979e` (concurrency, no other change) the run failed 2 of 14: the occupier control and the errno control read "it exited before announcing a listener … (nothing: the child wrote neither stdout nor stderr)" where the child had written `EADDRINUSE`. The neighbour harness diagnosed a death on the child's `exit` event, and Node does not order `exit` after this side has read the child's pipes, and with the cases running together the order flipped. The death is now diagnosed on `close` (both pipes drained); the liveness flag the probe loop reads still comes from `exit`. The same ordering is possible in the sequential file, only rarer.

## `@objectstack/rest`: first loads, and a reader materializing what no case reads

Two mechanisms, measured before either change:

1. **First loads in the first cases' clocks.** The first case read 359 to 431 ms against 36 to 114 ms for the same work later in the file (the route imports `exceljs` lazily in `xlsx-module.ts`, and the SQL driver, the template writer in both locales, the import door and the export writers each run cold once). `warmUpFirstLoads()` walks each path once at module scope on a throwaway engine and destroys it before the first case; every case still boots an engine of its own, and the warm-up shares no engine, row or spy with any case. Alone, it read 2090 and 2466 ms in 2 rounds whose base copies read 2837 and 2691 ms.
2. **The test's reader expands every dropdown into 50 000 entries.** exceljs's reader turns each range-keyed dataValidation element into one entry per covered cell, and the template covers `TEMPLATE_VALIDATED_ROWS` (50 000) rows per dropdown column. A probe on the `deal` template (10 parses each, after warming): 100 000 entries, 39.4 ms a parse in full, 4.4 ms with the node skipped through exceljs's own `ignoreNodes` read option, every sheet's values identical; on a one-column template 22.6 ms against 3.6 ms. No case in this file asserts on a dropdown, and `import-template.test.ts` pins the dropdowns, read in full. So this file's reads go through `readWorkbook` (the node skipped); the test loader `xlsx-test-loader.ts` gains an optional `options` argument handed straight to `Xlsx.load`, and its other six callers are unchanged. The one case that writes a workbook back for the import door ("is not starred …") still reads it in full, so the file it imports carries its dropdowns.

The parity case's budget (#21481, `PARITY_MS_PER_SHAPE`) is untouched; its docblock gains one sentence that the parse no longer reads the dropdowns.

## The warm-up docblock (`packages/verify/src/boot-warm-up.testkit.ts`)

"⛔ It shares nothing a case asserts on" is replaced by what a warm-up DOES leave to the file's own boots, why that is safe for a case that asserts on none of it, and which files therefore take no warm-up. What it leaves, from source and from a probe (an untracked file snapshotting the process around one `warmUpBoot()`):

- `harnessCryptoProvider()` in `harness.ts` builds the process's crypto provider on the first boot and keeps it (slice 4's ablation K is the measured consequence for `harness.key-custody`);
- `NODE_ENV`: `bootStack` sets `development` and never restores it; the probe's whole environment diff is `NODE_ENV: test -> development`;
- the loaded modules' process-level state: the module registry, sql.js's WASM, the JIT, better-auth's process-global context holder (the probe's one `globalThis` addition, `Symbol(better-auth:global)`), and each module's memos and once-per-process notices (from source: an environment variable memoized on first read in `metadata-protocol`, warn-once flags in `runtime` and `metadata-protocol`).
- Released, not shared: the configuration claim (`LIVE_CONFIGURATIONS` / `LIVE_APP_PLUGINS`, released by `stop()`) and `bootStackOnce`'s map (a warm-up never calls it). Process listeners: unchanged.
- "Under vitest's per-file isolation, the file's": two probe files in one run, `--maxWorkers=1`, read two pids, and a `globalThis` symbol one set was absent in the other.

## The six warmed files, read case by case for harness process state

| file | finding |
|:--|:--|
| `action-flow-elevated-door.test.ts` | none. Every case asserts the door's answer, the ledger rows and the run-log count on the file's own stack. The module code after the warm-up builds the fixture through `defineStack` / `ObjectSchema.create`, which read no `NODE_ENV`. No secret field, no provider, no notice is read. |
| `automation-trigger-elevated-door.test.ts` | none, the same shape at the trigger door. |
| `delete-behavior.test.ts` | none. Its two pure `deriveDeleteBehaviorCases` cases run before the file's first boot, so under `development` instead of `test` after the warm-up; the derivation reads the spec's `FieldSchema` and the package's collection reader, neither of which reads `NODE_ENV`. The proof cases read their own stacks' reports. |
| `handle.test.ts` | none. The tenancy cases read a posture `bootStack` requests and restores per boot (the warm-up boots `single` and sets nothing). The `bootStackOnce` identity case keys on `handleFixtureStack` and `BOOT_OPTIONS`; the warm-up boots its own configuration through `bootStack`, so that map holds nothing of it. |
| `harness.one-composition.test.ts` | none. The instance-rule cases key on configuration identity, and the warm-up's configuration is its own and released on `stop()` (slice 4's ablation O failed the same two cases with and without the warm-up). |
| `harness.served-composition.test.ts` | none. The cases read the plugins, the cube registry and the `sys_email` rows of each case's own stack; the SMTP case deletes and restores its environment variable around its own boot. |

No edit to any of the six was needed.

## Proof the changed files still fail when their subject breaks

Each mutation went through `scripts/ablation-replace.mjs` in wrap mode (anchor hit x1 → x0, blob moved), inside a script with an `EXIT INT TERM` trap; predictions were written before the runs; each restore was proven blob == HEAD and `git diff HEAD` empty. No `dist/` sits between these mutations and the runs: both suites read the mutated file from `src`.

- **R**: `import-template.ts`, the header loses its required ` *` (`header: required ? … : label,` → `header: label,`). Predicted 5 red, the same five on head and base. Observed head 5 failed / 32 passed, base copy 5 failed / 32 passed, the same five cases ("keeps exactly the writable declared fields", "?fields= is honoured", "create on the object and no allowExport", "is not starred …", the parity case). The lean reader sees exactly what the full one sees.
- **C**: `runBlock` answers status 0 for every block. Predicted 5 red. Observed 5 failed / 9 passed: both "refuses a neighbour", both "fails fast", and the docker "stops polling".

## Unchanged

- Every `it` / `describe` title line hashes the same at `af284b05e` and the head (`rest` 38 lines, `1765d3f3f8608dd2`; `create-objectstack` 15 lines, `cb0a2987aa6e987a` once the added options argument on the two suites is taken out), and `expect(` counts are equal (104 = 104, 39 = 39).
- No timeout, budget, project, roster entry or test moved; no test deleted.

## Tests and gates

- At `dafeb41ad` (this branch merged with `origin/main` `cbfa5e433`, after which only `257fe77d8`, a comment in `boot-warm-up.testkit.ts`, landed): `create-objectstack` 18 files / 278 tests passed and `tsc --noEmit` exit 0; `@objectstack/rest` (`--project local`) 294 files / 6030 passed, 326 skipped, and `typecheck` exit 0 (`check:test-typecheck` OK, 0 errors); `@objectstack/verify` 41 files / 362 tests passed and `typecheck` exit 0. Each changed file is in its package's type-check program (`--listFilesOnly`: 1 hit each).
- At `257fe77d8`: `node scripts/pm/dispatch-gates.mjs --commands --repo objectstack-ai/objectstack` derived 51 commands for the 4 paths (merge base `cbfa5e433`); all 51 exited 0 (`check:dual-build-cjs-loads` after a full `turbo run build`, which it refuses to measure without); `--ran`: "51 derived, 51 run, 0 NOT-MEASURED, 0 UNRUN."
- `pnpm exec eslint --no-inline-config` over the 4 changed files: exit 0. Control-byte scan over them: no hit. The repo-wide `pnpm lint`, `test:repo` (no `rest` repo-project test imports the loader) and every family CI runs are read from this PR's own check runs.

## Changeset

`skip-changeset`: `@objectstack/rest`, `@objectstack/verify` and `create-objectstack` each publish `dist`, `README.md` and `CHANGELOG.md`. After building all three, the strings this change introduces (`readWorkbook`, `warmUpFirstLoads`, `CASES_RUN_TOGETHER`, `ignoreNodes`, `loadXlsxWorkbook`, `xlsx-test-loader`, `warmUpBoot`, `boot-warm-up`, `What it shares`) hit none of those paths (grep exit 1); the controls `createRestApiPlugin`, `bootStackOnce` and `detectPackageManager` hit each package's `dist`.

## Acceptance notes

- **A file outside the claim's surface:** `packages/rest/src/xlsx-test-loader.ts`, the package's test-layer exceljs loader (not in any tsup entry), gains the optional read-options argument. Named for the seat to declare.
- **Observation, not filed:** the production import door (`parseXlsxToRows`) pays the same dropdown expansion on every uploaded template, about 35 ms a parse on this box for the `deal` template's two dropdown columns. A cost, not a defect class; no carrier.
- **Observation, not filed:** after a warm-up's `stop()` one `TCPServerWrap` resource remains (still one after a second warm-up, and no `net.Server` among the active handles), consistent with the last boot's listener still closing rather than a per-boot leak. Not characterized further.
- The docker case's 4.3 s here is two loop sleeps: on this box the dying container is read as running for one extra probe. It does not change the head's verdict, and it bounds the file's concurrent wall.
